forecasts.question: Will a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange (strikes both ways) occur in any 48h window before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: IDF struck Hezbollah infrastructure in Dahieh/Beirut on June 14 after Hezbollah drone fire on northern Israel; Iran's Supreme National Security Council warned a response was 'imminent.' US diplomatic intervention prevented Iranian retaliation, and by June 15 Gharibabadi announced a permanent ceasefire on all fronts via IRIB/Tasnim. The MOU framework creates strong mutual disincentives for direct Iran-Israel exchanges through EOD June 24. June 14 exchange was proxy-based (Hezbollah vs IDF) and does not meet YES criteria. Ceasefire substantially reduces probability but does not eliminate spoiler risk from IRGC hardliners or further Israeli action.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange — Israeli strikes on Iranian targets AND Iranian strikes on Israeli/Israeli-claimed targets — within any rolling 48h window between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera) OR one TIER1 + official Israeli (IDF) or Iranian (IRGC) statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Proxy-only attacks (Hezbollah/Houthi) without direct Iran-Israel state strikes do NOT count; one-directional strikes within the 48h window = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: IDF + IRGC reciprocal strike statements within 48h
indicators.expected_effect: +30pp toward YES if bilateral direct exchange confirmed

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: As of June 7 (latest AIS data), commercial transits ~2 ships/day vs baseline ~94. MOU calls for Hormuz reopening but formal signing not until June 19; Iranian side explicitly couples reopening to US fulfilling preliminary commitments with the Switzerland ceremony as start point. Even in the most optimistic scenario (signing June 19, IRGC immediate compliance), reaching a 7-day average of 50 commercial transits before EOD July 2 (~13 days from signing) requires mine clearance, P&I insurer confidence restoration, and operator willingness — an extraordinary ramp that physical and actuarial constraints do not support.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

indicators.name: PortWatch 7-day transit trend rising above 10 transits/day
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; leading indicator for trajectory

forecasts.question: Will mine-countermeasure clearing operations actively commence in Hormuz before EOD 2026-07-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Operation Project Freedom (MCM component) commenced April-May 2026 but Trump paused it May 5-6. No confirmed MCM resumption as of early June. The June 14-15 MOU announcement substantially changes calculus: the MOU framework includes Hormuz reopening as a core deliverable and Pentagon/CENTCOM will face strong pressure to resume MCM as a concrete commitment. Horizon is July 10 — 25 days from today and ~21 days from the Switzerland signing. DA's hunting-vs-clearing distinction is valid: 'commencement' per spec requires TIER1 confirmation of actual clearing operations, not merely minehunting/detection. Judge chose 0.45 rather than Analyst's 0.55 to reflect this uncertainty gap.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports mine-countermeasure vessels/operations have actively commenced clearing the Strait of Hormuz (US/coalition/third-party) between 2026-06-10 and 2026-07-10.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/CNBC, or a named US/UK/coalition naval/Pentagon statement carried by TIER1.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Stated intent, vessel positioning, or planning without confirmed commencement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Minehunting (detection/survey) without confirmed clearing commencement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: TIER1/Pentagon report of MCM clearing operations commencing (not just minehunting)
indicators.expected_effect: +30pp toward YES; direct resolution trigger distinguishing clearing from detection

indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; corroborating indicator of operational MCM progress

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: Dissolution bill passed first reading 106-0 on June 1. No date set for second and third readings; no election date agreed upon. With US-Iran MOU announced June 14-15, Netanyahu now has a potential diplomatic-victory framing that reduces his incentive to rush dissolution. Haredi-coalition disagreement on draft exemption bill remains unresolved. July 15 deadline is technically reachable if readings are scheduled in next four weeks, but Netanyahu's political calculus has shifted toward delay. DA's 0.20-0.25 is too pessimistic given legislation can advance on its own momentum; Judge chooses 0.35.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will the US-Iran MOU be formally signed in Switzerland (or equivalent venue) before EOD 2026-06-21?
forecasts.delta_reason: Both US and Iranian sides (Gharibabadi via Tasnim; Pakistan PM Sharif; Trump) announced MOU text finalized and signing scheduled in Switzerland June 19. Nine TIER1 sources confirm agreement text. Spoiler risk ~25%: IRGC hardliners, renewed Israeli strikes before signing (IDF struck Beirut June 14, nearly derailing the announcement), US domestic opposition, or last-minute Iranian walkback given Fars News/Kayhan framing divergence on Hormuz control and nuclear commitments.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports that a formal signing ceremony for the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding occurred at a named venue before EOD 2026-06-21, with named signatories from both the US and Iranian sides.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters, AP, AFP, CNN, NBC, CBS, Al Jazeera, Times of Israel, or a State Dept/Iran MFA joint statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: A unilateral announcement of 'deal reached' without a formal signing ceremony = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A signing after EOD June 21 resolves NO regardless of proximity. A signing at a venue other than Switzerland counts as YES if TIER1-confirmed with named principals from both sides.

forecasts.question: Will commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz resume at a rate exceeding 20 transits per day (3-day average) before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: US-Iran MOU framework explicitly calls for Hormuz to reopen following June 19 signing. Iranian Deputy FM stated blockade lift begins upon signing. Lower threshold (20 transits/day, 3-day average) than F4's 50/day and longer horizon (July 15 vs July 2) allows for realistic ramp timeline. Mine clearance, P&I insurer confidence, and IRGC compliance all create lag between formal ceasefire and actual commercial traffic restoration. Symmetric uncertainty — balanced at 0.45.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if AIS/PortWatch records a 3-day average of at least 20 commercial vessel transits per day through the Strait of Hormuz at any point between 2026-06-15 and 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch, MarineTraffic, VesselsValue, or equivalent AIS data carried by TIER1 (Reuters/Bloomberg/Lloyd's List/Al Jazeera).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted vessels without commercial cargo designation do not count. US military transits alone do not count. Single-day spikes below a 3-day average do not qualify. Iranian state-controlled tankers transiting count if commercially designated in AIS.
